title: Zucca al Forno
subtitle: Roasted butternut squash with olive oil, garlic, and sage
excerpt: Butternut squash cut into wedges and roasted until the edges caramelise and the flesh is completely tender. Garlic and sage go in halfway through so they crisp without burning. A side dish that needs almost no effort.
sourceNotes: Italian roasted squash preparation. Synthesised from autumn vegetable cooking traditions common across northern and central Italy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast up to 2 hours ahead and serve at room temperature. Do not cover or the caramelised edges soften.

content.text: Roasting concentrates the squash's natural sweetness. Leave the skin on if it is thin; it becomes edible and helps the pieces hold together. Watch the garlic and sage after you add them, as they can go from golden to burnt quickly.

items.prepNote: about 1kg, peeled, seeds removed, cut into 3cm wedges

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Put the roasting tin in the oven to get hot while you prepare the squash.
Toss the squash wedges in the olive oil, salt, pepper, and chilli flakes if using. Make sure every piece is coated.
Carefully tip the squash into the hot tin. Spread in a single layer, cut side down. The tin should sizzle when the squash goes in.
Roast for 20 minutes without moving the squash. This lets the cut surface caramelise rather than steam.
Add the garlic cloves and sage leaves to the tin. Turn the squash pieces over. Roast for a further 15 to 20 minutes until tender and deep golden at the edges.
Check that the squash is soft all the way through with a small knife. If not, give it 5 minutes more.
Arrange on a serving plate. Squeeze the roasted garlic from its skin over the squash if you like, and scatter the crisp sage leaves on top.

items.symptom: The squash is soft but pale with no colour.
items.cause: The tin was cold when the squash went in, or pieces were too close together.
items.fix: Spread pieces out more and switch to a higher shelf for the last 10 minutes.

items.cause: They went in too early or the oven runs hot.
items.fix: Add the sage in the last 8 minutes only, or skip it and finish with a drizzle of good olive oil.

items.symptom: The squash sticks to the tin.
items.cause: Not enough oil or the caramelisation is still in progress.
items.fix: Leave it for 2 minutes more. Properly caramelised squash releases cleanly. Force it and it tears.
